opening_message:
Ticket 1: Kim Dunn (employee ID E048) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E048.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: Kim Dunn (E048), Engineer, full-time. Requested admin to Source Code. Full-time Engineer owns Source Code, so admin is permitted per policy.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E048 (Kim Dunn) is a contractor with basic security training (HR note listed full-time — discrepancy). Contractors max at read without advanced training; admin is never permitted. Recommend read for Source Code.
reason: HR's database (the system of record for employment type) lists Kim Dunn (E048) as a full-time Engineer. Under policy, full-time employees may have admin if their role owns the system, and the Engineer role owns Source Code. The requested level (admin) is at the maximum allowed, so admin is granted. Note: Security's DB shows contractor, creating a discrepancy, but I am relying on HR as authoritative for employment status; role is confirmed by both agents.

Discrepancy: HR says full-time, Security says contractor.

Access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the employee's role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Source Code is owned by Engineer role. If full-time Engineer: admin is permitted (role owns system). If contractor: never admin.
